finding.title: Reuse trackDeletionAllowed() in TrackDetailScreen._showDeleteDialog instead of re-deriving the TRK-HUB-04 guard inline
finding.rule: Evans (invariant re-derived, not enforced in one place) / Fowler-duplication
finding.why: track_management_hub_screen.dart defines the pure, unit-tested trackDeletionAllowed() specifically to centralize the 'never delete the profile's last active curriculum' rule (TS-16/TRK-HUB-04) and calls it from its own delete dialog. track_detail_screen.dart's delete dialog implements an equivalent-but-separate `<= 1` check inline, twice (once as a pre-check, once again before the wipe path) — it never calls the tested helper. track_hub_ts16_test.dart (in this batch) reads as though it validates 'the' Archive/Delete dialog's guard, but it only protects the hub screen's call site; TrackDetailScreen's independent re-implementation could silently diverge (e.g. someone changes the hub's threshold to `< 1` for a policy change, updates trackDeletionAllowed and its test, and never notices track_detail_screen.dart's two untouched inline copies now disagree) without any test catching the drift.
finding.recommendation: Replace both inline `activeCurricula.length <= 1` / `activeCount.length <= 1` checks in track_detail_screen.dart with calls to trackDeletionAllowed(activeCurriculumCount: ...). Add a TrackDetailScreen-level widget test asserting the same last-curriculum boundary track_hub_ts16_test.dart already covers for the hub screen.
acceptance_criteria: track_detail_screen.dart's two inline `<= 1` checks are replaced with trackDeletionAllowed(...)

A widget test on TrackDetailScreen's delete flow (sole active curriculum) asserts the last-curriculum explanation shows and Archive/Wipe are withheld, independent of track_management_hub_screen coverage

finding.title: De-duplicate the TrackDetailScreen dual-progress and bulk-prior-tile assertions shared by track_detail_screen_test.dart and edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart
finding.why: Two independent files pin the identical TrackDetailScreen behaviors — the zero-valued dual-progress labels and the bulk-prior tile's outlined/tileColor styling — with near line-for-line matching assertions. This is dead weight, not extra protection: any copy or styling change must be updated in two places using two different fixture-building helpers (_overridesFor vs _buildDetailApp), and it contributes ~200 of edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart's 1733 lines to content that already has a dedicated, purpose-built home. It also obscures which file is the canonical owner of TrackDetailScreen coverage going forward.
finding.recommendation: Keep track_detail_screen_test.dart (the Task #16-scoped file) as the sole owner of dual-progress/bulk-prior-tile assertions; delete the duplicate groups from edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart, retaining only scenarios unique to the combined edit+detail flow (B-EDIT-NAME title propagation across navigation, min-1-curriculum delete gating, chazara header wiring).
acceptance_criteria: Only one test file asserts 'Track progress: 0%'/'Lifetime: 0%' and the bulk-prior tile's shape/tileColor properties
make test-story/epic runs for tracks/setup still pass after consolidation with no coverage loss for the removed duplicate assertions

finding.title: Register StartingPositionCalendarMode with the shared expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices harness instead of the ad hoc single-viewport check

evidence.quote:
// To add a new dialog/screen to the guard, add a `testWidgets` case in
// `test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart` that calls this helper

finding.why: The repo already built and documented expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices specifically for this class of regression (RenderFlex overflow at extreme device/text-scale corners), with an explicit extension point at test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart. StartingPositionCalendarMode — the exact widget that shipped a 'BOTTOM OVERFLOWED BY 59 PIXELS' bug — was never added there (grepped test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart for 'StartingPositionCalendarMode'/'Starting': no match). Instead this batch's test hand-rolls a single fixed corner (375×500 @ 2.0x text scale) and asserts on implementation details (a SingleChildScrollView exists; no Spacer exists) rather than the systematic multi-corner check the rest of the codebase relies on. A future edit that reintroduces overflow at a different corner (e.g. the narrow 280×653 or 1.3x scale the shared matrix covers) would ship undetected by this file, and the general-purpose guard would never learn about this widget either.
finding.recommendation: Add a testWidgets case for StartingPositionCalendarMode to test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart using expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices with the required provider overrides; keep or retire the structural (SingleChildScrollView/Spacer) assertions as a secondary, narrower regression check if desired.
acceptance_criteria: test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart includes a case pumping StartingPositionCalendarMode through expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices across the default device/text-scale matrix

finding.title: Tighten the granularity and pace-floor assertions in step_chazara_goal_l1_test.dart and edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart to match what their own titles/comments claim

evidence.quote:
// Just verifying the value "1" is visible (loading completed).
        expect(find.text('1'), findsWidgets);

finding.why: The chazara-goal test titled 'selecting coarse (perek) emits paceGranularity=perek' taps the 'Perakim' segment then only asserts goal.rawLearningUnit isNotNull — but _paceGranularity is set to a non-null default in initState() before any tap, so the assertion passes identically whether or not the tap actually changed anything. The edit-track test titled 'pace increment button is disabled when paceValue is 1 (minimum)' never inspects the stepper button's onPressed at all (its own comment admits 'Just verifying the value "1" is visible') — floor enforcement for EditTrackScreen's pace stepper is untested anywhere in the tree (grepped for 'remove_rounded'/'onPressed.*isNull' in the sibling edit_track_screen_l1_test.dart: no match).
finding.recommendation: Assert goal.rawLearningUnit equals the coarse key's storage value ('perek') rather than isNotNull. In the edit-track test, find the decrement IconButton (ancestor of Icons.remove_rounded) and assert its onPressed is null at paceValue==1, then non-null after an increment.
acceptance_criteria: Granularity test asserts goal.rawLearningUnit == the expected coarse key, not just non-null
Pace-floor test asserts tester.widget<IconButton>(...).onPressed is null at value 1 and non-null after incrementing

finding.title: Split the four tracks/setup test files over the 400-line AG-3 cap

evidence.quote: /// Regression tests for the Track Detail screen (W5-B / Task #16).
// L1 widget tests — ChazaraReadOnlyStep + SelfPacedGoalStep (uncovered branches)
// L1 widget-behaviour tests — ScopeStepContent + ScopeTopLevelView + ScopeHierarchyView

finding.why: edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart is 1733 lines (4.3x the cap), step_chazara_goal_l1_test.dart is 1015, step_scope_l1_test.dart is 986, and track_detail_screen_test.dart is 578 — all hand-written, none generated. AG-3 applies repo-wide to hand-written Dart including tests; no Rule-0 checker currently enforces it (grepped tool/ and both Makefiles: no 400-line check exists). Large files raise review cost and, for edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart specifically, compound with Finding 4's duplication (splitting by screen would naturally surface and remove the overlap).
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its own documented section boundaries (e.g. edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart already separates into 'EditTrackScreen' and 'TrackDetailScreen' halves via its own comments — split along that line, reconciling with Finding 4). Add a tool/ script or make target that fails when a hand-written lib/ or test/ .dart file exceeds 400 lines.
acceptance_criteria: The four listed files are each ≤400 lines or split into cohesive ≤400-line files along existing section boundaries
A checker (script or make target) greps hand-written .dart files for line count >400 and exits non-zero with file:line, excluding generated (*.g.dart, *.freezed.dart) globs
